name: Congruence Equation
description: Given an integer $$$x$$$. Your task is to find out how many positive integers $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq x$$$) satisfy $$$$$$n \cdot a^n \equiv b \quad (\textrm{mod}\;p),$$$$$$ where $$$a, b, p$$$ are all known constants.
input_specification: The only line contains four integers $$$a,b,p,x$$$ ($$$2 \leq p \leq 10^6+3$$$, $$$1 \leq a,b \lt p$$$, $$$1 \leq x \leq 10^{12}$$$). It is guaranteed that $$$p$$$ is a prime.
output_specification: Print a single integer: the number of possible answers $$$n$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) paradigm under the Number Theory framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
